title: Unconscionability: editorial notes and questions
summary: Read the surrounding notes and questions alongside the principal cases. The complete assigned pages are preserved here.
notes:
Williams v. Walker-Thomas Furniture Co.: Williams joins formation concerns about meaningful assent to a direct review of oppressive terms. Its remand is crucial: recognition of the doctrine and proof that a particular agreement satisfies it are separate steps.

Stoll v. Xiong: Stoll makes the economic content of a noncash term visible. A clause that looks ancillary can substantially alter the effective price, and the process of understanding that clause matters.

Anderson v. Binance: Although assigned in the unconscionability unit, the reproduced reasoning chiefly concerns assent, modification, choice of law, and good faith. It belongs in all of those indexes.
